user_scenario: You are Claire Beaudoin, a 52-year-old retired French-immersion teacher from Ottawa who rents out her two-bedroom condo near Disney Springs, outside Orlando, on Roamhaven. You are calm, organised and a little formal on the phone, and you prefer short answers. In August a guest cracked the sliding glass patio door; you filed a HostCover claim, and this morning an email told you Roamhaven approved it and that the reimbursement was credited to your payouts. Your contractor in Kissimmee wants to be paid before he installs the new door, and your next guests checked in yesterday. You open the call by saying you would like whatever Roamhaven can pay you right now sent to your PayPal account today, instead of waiting for next Monday's weekly payout. You have only the one payout method, your PayPal account in Canadian dollars, and that is where the money should go; you are asking for a payout now, nothing else. You do not volunteer your details: only when the agent asks you to confirm who you are do you give your registered mobile number, 6135554271, and the last four characters of your passport, 4630, and only if the agent needs one more detail do you add your date of birth, 1974-06-18, or your email, claire.beaudoin@sympatico.ca. If the agent asks how much you expect, you say you honestly do not know — the email only mentioned roughly twelve hundred dollars for the door — and that you are happy with whatever the rules allow today. If the agent explains that something has to be posted on your payout account before the money can go, or that part of the balance has to stay for the regular Monday payout, you accept it calmly and tell them to go ahead. When the agent sends you the payout confirmation to approve in your host app, you approve it with exactly the payout method, the host account reference and the amount the agent read out to you, and you read back the confirmation you see. Once you hear that the payout has been sent, you thank the agent and end the call.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.payout_method_id: 0d46fb27-23a8-4cba-93e8-2ed750e3b3be. Basis: the conversion-fee rule says the fee is 'booked as a cross_currency_fee against that method' — the method the transfer was sent to; the ledger row of the 2026-09-14 transfer carries payout_method_id 0d46fb27-23a8-4cba-93e8-2ed750e3b3be, the only method she holds (find_payout_methods). Unique: there is no other method.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.source_event_id: d827a2eb-98bf-4fed-a1cd-024b45c0a3d1. Basis: the rule books the fee 'naming the transfer it belongs to'; the fee 'falls due on the transfer's settlement day, processing_business_days business days ... after the day the transfer was sent' — PayPal processing_business_days is 1, so the 2026-09-14 transfer settles on 2026-09-15, the request date, and the ledger shows no cross_currency_fee naming it, while every earlier transfer already has its fee. Unique: it is the only transfer whose fee is due and unbooked; the 2026-09-01 and earlier fees exist.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: 4.05. Conversion volume over 12 months 15087.59 >= 8000.00 in CAD -> rate 1.25; 659.40 x 1.25 % = 8.242500 (cap 20.00 not reached); the transfer is between 250.00 and 999.99, so the charge is the greater of that and the 9.00 minimum = 9.00; combined discount 25 (Superhost 29 months) + 5 (Rewards Gold) + 10 (method on file 36 months) + 15 (account open 67 months) = 55 percent applied once -> 4.0500 -> rounded half up -> 4.05.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.payout_method_id: 0d46fb27-23a8-4cba-93e8-2ed750e3b3be. Basis: the on-request payout 'is sent as one transfer to that method' — the active method whose balance is paid; she asked for the money to go to her PayPal, her only method. Unique: no other method exists.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.host_account_id: 241e50b7-c5ec-4e85-9dc1-3c3aa32b59bf. Basis: find_host_accounts returns her single host account, the account the method belongs to (payout_methods.host_account_id); the tool asks for the host account the method belongs to. Balance after the 4.05 fee = 2287.21 (release 1037.90 - premium 12.04 + reimbursement 1265.40 - fee 4.05, earlier items swept); fresh share 80 (rating 4.86, 14 stays) + 4 (response 97.50) = 84 -> holdback 1037.90 x 16 / 100 = 166.064; claim advance 50 (HostCover Plus) x 0.80 = 40 -> holdback 759.24; float = largest fee ever charged 14.4 (16 transfers in 12 months); 2287.21 - 166.064 - 759.24 - 14.4 = 1347.506 -> rounded half up 1347.51.

edges.condition: Every payout_sent row of the method whose settlement day (processing_business_days business days after its posted_date) is on or before the request date, and which was not returned before that day, has a payout_fee_charged row with fee_type cross_currency_fee whose source_event_id names it — required only when the method's payout_currency is not USD and its rail's cross_currency_fee_pct is above 0.00; on any other method no conversion fee falls due and the condition holds as it stands.
edges.policy_source: An on-request payout is fixed only after every conversion fee falling due on the method's transfers by the request date stands on the method's ledger.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The PayPal method is paid in CAD (processing_business_days 1); the 2026-09-14 transfer settles on 2026-09-15, the request date, so its conversion fee is due, and no payout_fee_charged row names it.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The conversion-fee booking adds a payout_fee_charged row (fee_type cross_currency_fee, source_event_id d827a2eb-98bf-4fed-a1cd-024b45c0a3d1, amount 4.05); the balance the payout draws on falls from 2291.26 to 2287.21.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A single prerequisite edge: the conversion fee is booked first, the on-request payout last; there are no parallel prerequisites to reorder.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the conversion fee leaves the balance at 2291.26 and the payout at 1351.56 instead of 1347.51; the terminal ledger also lacks the 4.05 fee row.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario speaks only of the HostCover reimbursement approved that morning, the stay that began the day before and her wish to have what can be sent go to her PayPal today; it never mentions a conversion fee, the 2026-09-14 transfer's settlement or any fee booking, and gives no hint that something must be settled first.

design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — host_payouts task 0 (on-request payout of a PayPal CAD balance). Revision 3 (after audits r1 and r2).

[0. Draw and scope snapshot] draw_counts.py --task 0 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 1, "factor_counts": [6, 5]}. Tree: root payout_ext_on_request_payout (5 factors, owner=user tool send_on_request_payout_d225f921) <- payout_ext_conversion_fee (6 factors, agent tool book_conversion_fee_3c5b00cd). Occupied before this task: nothing. Claimed here: those two policies and two tools. Left for task 1 (draw: 2 prerequisite problems, factors [5,4,5]): the return charge, the transfer fee and the host-confirmed re-send of a returned transfer.

[1. Why this is a good test] The host only says "send what you can pay me now to my PayPal". The figure she confirms is the PayPal balance less two holdbacks and a float, and it waits on a fee the ledger does not show yet. The agent must (a) read the on-request rule's prerequisite sentence "An on-request payout is fixed only after every conversion fee falling due on the method's transfers by the request date stands on the method's ledger.", (b) see that the 2026-09-14 transfer d827a2eb-98bf-4fed-a1cd-024b45c0a3d1 settles on 2026-09-15 (PayPal processing_business_days 1) with no cross_currency_fee while every earlier transfer has one, (c) find in the conversion-fee rule the write that books it, compute it through six factors and book it, then (d) reconcile the ledger and apply five more factors read from the host ledger, HostCover and the method's own history.

[2. Factor card — conversion fee (expected 4.05, baseline_result 13.19)]
- conv_volume_corridor_rate (parameter, multi-source currency AND 12-month ledger volume): CAD and 15087.59 >= 8000.00 -> 1.25 percent; rail 2.00 -> 5.93.
- conv_charge_structure (method — how the conversion charge is formed, as FX providers price small conversions: a flat charge below 250.00, the greater of the percentage charge and a 9.00 minimum from 250.00 to 999.99, the percentage charge alone from 1000.00): the named transfer 659.40 -> greater of 8.2425 and 9.00 = 9.00; percentage alone -> 3.71.
- conv_superhost_discount (parameter, cross-difficulty host): Superhost 29 months -> 25; none -> 6.3.
- conv_rewards_discount (parameter, rewards): Rewards Gold -> 5; none -> 4.5.
- conv_long_held_method_discount (parameter): method on file 36 months -> 10; none -> 4.95.
- conv_account_tenure_discount (parameter, cross-difficulty host): account open 67 months -> 15; none -> 5.4.
A single half-up rounding at the end, as the charter's fee_rounding prescribes.
Factor card — on-request payout (expected 1347.51, baseline_result 556.65)
- onreq_fresh_earnings_share (parameter, host; both conditions are fields of one assessment row, so it is not counted as multi-source): 2026-07-01 assessment 4.86 / 14 stays -> 80; baseline 60 -> 1139.93. Near-miss: the 2026-04-01 assessment (4.91 / 99.20) is not the most recent.
- onreq_responsiveness_bonus (parameter, host): response 97.50 -> +4; none -> 1305.99
- onreq_claim_advance_share (parameter, cross-difficulty protect): HostCover Plus -> 50; none -> 841.35
- onreq_claim_history (parameter, protect): 2 reimbursements in 24 months -> x0.80; x1 -> 1474.05
- onreq_float_rule (method: largest fee ever / percentage of the pre-float balance / flat amount): 16 transfers in 12 months -> largest fee ever 14.40; flat 50.00 -> 1311.91
The task's multi-source factor is conv_volume_corridor_rate; cross-difficulty factors read host and protect rows seeded for this customer.

[3. Base-invariant card] Fee write (payout_fee_charged): governed by payout_evt_transfer and payout_evt_returns_and_reactivation, whose gates apply to payout_sent / payout_method_reactivated only -> policy_scope. Payout write (payout_sent): method_active, account_not_suspended, new_method_hold (anchor verified_date 2023-08-21, PayPal 3 calendar days, inclusive: 2023-08-24 waits, 2023-08-25 allowed; frozen 2026-09-15 passes).

[4. Business-object card] Method 0d46fb27-23a8-4cba-93e8-2ed750e3b3be (PayPal, CAD, default). The fee names transfer d827a2eb-98bf-4fed-a1cd-024b45c0a3d1 (posted 2026-09-14, 659.40), the only transfer whose settlement day is the request date and which lacks a fee. Open items on the request date: release 1037.90 of the stay checked in 2026-09-14, its HostCover premium 12.04, the patio-door claim reimbursement 1265.40. Opening balance 2291.26; after the fee 2287.21.

[5. Problem-tree card] Edge root -> payout_ext_conversion_fee, value_input on onreq_balance, form state; sentence passes the four-point test (only after; record-visible state; no tool/id/code token; hard strength over fees falling due by the request date). Condition (revised for CG-1): a cross_currency_fee is required only on a non-USD method whose rail charges one, and only for transfers not returned before settling — exactly the conversion rule's own exclusions. Only the conversion-fee policy's write creates cross_currency_fee rows. Seed falseness: d827a2eb-98bf-4fed-a1cd-024b45c0a3d1 posted 2026-09-14 on a PayPal CAD method with no fee row naming it. Order: fee, then payout. Skipping the fee: payout 1351.56 instead of 1347.51. The persona names no fee; no tool checks for fee rows.

[6. Seed design] 23 stays (guest profiles withheld from the host-side record), 23 releases, 23 premium deductions with their HostCover premium records, 2 claim reimbursement credits with claims and HostCover records, 23 weekly sweeps and 22 conversion fees re-derived for revision 2 under the revised schedule as it stood on each settlement day (no half-cent ties), 3 Superhost assessments, 23 host-fee assessments, Rewards Gold, HostCover Plus, the listing. No automatic clause fires (stay checked in, plan active, no hold, no return, W-8 on file).

[7. Persona] Claire Beaudoin, formal and brief; volunteers only the goal, the claim-approval email and the new check-in; gives phone 6135554271 and passport last four 4630 when asked; approves the in-app confirmation with the method, the host account reference and the amount read out; ends when told it was sent.

[8. Standard solution] find_customers(name) -> verify -> host account -> methods -> PayPal ledger -> host ledger -> Rewards -> HostCover plan, events, claims -> listing -> stays -> book conversion fee 4.05 on d827a2eb-98bf-4fed-a1cd-024b45c0a3d1 -> host confirms 1347.51 to the PayPal method for her host account.

[9. Verification] A temporary replica of check_compute (removed after closing; check_compute.py recomputes the same figures) printed fee 4.05 (baseline 13.19), payout 1347.51 (baseline 556.65), payout with the fee skipped 1351.56, and flagged no half-cent tie in any declared figure (each recomputed unrounded). Gates with --task 0 and without: EXTENDED OK, TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK, SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK, GROUNDING OK, SCOPE OK.

[10. Revision log, audit r1 (the volume-window factor named here was replaced in revision 3, see 10b)] CG-1: the on-request edge's condition restated with the conversion rule's exclusions (zero-pct rail, USD, returned before settling). CG-2: the tenure-keyed rounding ladder removed; the method factor is now the volume window convention by method age, account age became an additive discount (parameter), and the fee carries one half-up rounding — the overwrite of the base fee_rounding clause is withdrawn. O-1: the rule now says the fee is booked on the settlement day and every month count runs to that day. O-6/O-7: the on-request float tier no longer rounds on its own; the phrase "so the amount worked out here ..." replaced by "the amount the host confirms is the amount set out below". O-T0-1: the multi-source claim for the fresh share withdrawn above. O-T0-2: the response-bonus mid tier moved to 4 points so no declared figure lands on a half-cent tie (previous gold 1361.265 was one). O-T0-3: persona approval line names the host account reference. Downstream: whole ledger re-simulated (fee amounts and the sweeps after them), gold, computations, tracing, closure and contract re-derived.

[10b. Revision log, audit r2] CG-4: the volume-window factor was a lookback length (a parameter) labelled method; it is removed and the volume window is a fixed 12 whole months again. The conversion fee's method factor is now conv_charge_structure — how the conversion charge is formed by transfer size (flat charge / greater of percentage and a minimum / percentage alone), the way FX providers price small conversions; three different formulas, not three numbers in one formula. The small-transfer handling charge (also keyed on transfer size) is dropped so no two factors share a condition, and the long-held method discount (method age, now unused elsewhere) is restored as a parameter, keeping 6 factors (5 parameter + 1 method). O-7: "the amount set out below" -> "the amount this rule gives". Ledger re-simulated again (22 conversion fees and the sweeps after them), gold, computations, tracing, closure and seed checks re-derived. Task 1's policies, world and gold are untouched by this revision.

[11. Draft recomputation from visible context] 659.40 x 1.25 % = 8.2425, below the 9.00 minimum for a transfer between 250.00 and 999.99 -> 9.00; less 55 percent = 4.05 -> 4.05; balance 2291.26 - 4.05 = 2287.21; holdbacks 166.064 and 759.24, float 14.4 -> 1347.506 -> 1347.51. Agrees with gold.
